# messengerr command reference

<!-- GENERATED by build/generate_commands.rb from `messengerr` 0.2.0's own output.
     Do not edit by hand: CI regenerates this file from that exact version and fails on any difference. -->

Generated from **messengerr 0.2.0**.

## Top level

```
Usage: messengerr <command>

Commands:
  credentials  Manage integration credentials (setup|list|verify|delete)
  send         Send a message to a CSV contact list (see `send --help`)
  integrations List registered integrations
```

## credentials

Run bare, the command prints its usage (and exits 1). Claude never runs `setup` or `delete`: the human does.

```
Usage: messengerr credentials setup|list|verify|delete [--purge]
```

## send

```
Usage: messengerr send [flags]
        --method METHOD              Delivery method (skips the chooser)
        --integration NAME           Integration to use (e.g. postmark, clicksend)
        --dry-run                    Preview the rendered messages; send nothing
        --csv PATH                   Contact CSV (skips the path prompt)
        --contact COLUMN             Column holding the email/phone contact value
        --map PLACEHOLDER=COLUMN     Map a {{placeholder}} to a CSV column (repeatable)
        --message TEXT               Message body as a literal argument
        --subject TEXT               Email subject line ({{placeholders}} allowed)
        --allow-non-interactive      Send without an interactive terminal (human scripts only)
        --resume LEDGER              Skip recipients already sent in this ledger (row + contact)
        --ledger PATH                Where to record results (default: ./messengerr-ledger-<time>.jsonl)
        --batch-size N               Messages per batch
        --rate-limit N               Batches per second
        --from ADDRESS               Override the sender address/ID
        --message-file FILE          Read a multi-line plain-text message from FILE instead of typing one line
        --html FILE                  Send FILE as an HTML email (email only; HTML only, no text version)
    -h, --help                       Show this help
```

Most flags **answer a wizard question in advance**; anything left out is still asked. `dry_run.sh` never prompts, so give it every flag.

Placeholders in the message and the subject each need a `--map placeholder=column`.

## integrations

```
email:
  postmark — not configured
sms:
  clicksend — not configured
```

(Shown with an empty configuration; on a real machine each integration says `configured` once its credentials are stored.)

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Everything was sent, or a `--dry-run` completed. |
| `1` | Some sends failed, the run was aborted, or an error stopped it (printed as `messengerr: ...`). |
| `130` | The send was interrupted with Ctrl-C. The ledger and a `--resume` command are printed. |

## The send guard

A send that is not a `--dry-run` is refused unless standard input is an interactive terminal:

```
messengerr: refusing to send without an interactive terminal: run `messengerr send` yourself in a terminal (or pass --allow-non-interactive in your own scripts). --dry-run works anywhere.
```

That is the intended behaviour for Claude and for CI: Claude prepares and previews, the human sends. `--allow-non-interactive` exists for the human's own scripts and is never used by this skill.
